The Police Sub-Inspector of Sanjay Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Section 285, 420 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 7(1)(a) of Essential Commodities Act and Sec.7, 3(1)(a), 3(b)(c), 6, 4(1)(a) of Gas Supply Act, 2000.

2. Prosecution Case: On 19-10-2021 at House No.348, 3rd Main Road, Basaveshwara Layout, within the limits of Sanjay Nagara Police Station, the accused without obtaining license possessed domestic and commercial gas cylinders of various gas companies unauthorisedly and was refilling to other gas cylinders without adhering to safety measures with an intention to make wrongful gain thereby cheated the Government as well as customers.
3. First Information Report: CW1/PW1

Sri Subramani, PSI of Sanjay Nagara PS, Bengaluru on the receipt of credible information, raided the house bearing No.348, 3rd Main Road, Basaveshwara Layout, Nagashettihalli, Bangalore along with pancha witnesses, staff and found that the accused was refilling the domestic gas to other gas cylinders and hence the accused was taken into custody and conducted spot cum seizure mahazar as per Ex.P1 from 10:20 am to 11:30 am and seized rubber pipe, valve, refilling machine, 3 domestic cylinders of an Indane company, one domestic cylinder of Subramani M Psi vs Rafeeq Ali on 29 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120386314/
2 Bharat company, two cylinders weighing 5 kg, three cylinders weighing 3 kg, two cylinders weighing 2 kg, weighing machine and produced the same before CW9 and Ex.P2 report was given.

sentences.text: The seized properties were handed over to the Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department by obtaining permission from the court.
4. Investigation:

During the course of investigation, on receipt of report from CW1, PW7 Sri Ravhichandra, PSI, registered FIR as per Ex.P2, subjected the properties under PF No.101/2021,
recorded the statements of CW2 to CW8, obtained a report from CW6 as per Ex.P4 on seized cylinders, the items seized were handed over to the Food Department, after investigation he filed charge sheet against the accused.
5. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court had taken cognizance of offences alleged against the accused.
6. Copies of prosecution paper as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.
7. The accused was released on bail at the pre- cognizance stage by the order dated 21-10-2021.
8. Charge:

After hearing learned APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable under Section 285, 420 of IPC and Sec.7 of E.C. Act and Sec.3, 6 and 7 of Gas Supply order, 2000 has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 9 witnesses examined all witnesses and exhibited 10 documents and closed their side.
The presence of CW2 could not be secured and hence dropped out from examination despite due execution of proclamation by the order dated 11/08/2023.
On account of examination of CW7, the examination of CW8 was given up by the order dated 20/08/2025.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of Cr.P.C: After completion of evidence of prosecution, the accused was examined as per section 313 statement of Cr.P.C wherein he denied all incriminating evidence appearing in the statement of prosecution witnesses and did not lead any rebuttal evidence.
11.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 19-10-2021 at House bearing No.348, 3rd Main Road, Basaveshwara Layout, within the limits of Sanjay Nagara Police Station, the accused without obtaining license possessed gas cylinders and was refilling to other cylinders without adhering to safety measures thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable U/sec.285 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on above said date, time and place, the accused without obtaining license possessed domestic gas cylinders unauthorisedly and was refilling to gas cylinders without adhering to safety measures with an intention to make wrongful gains thereby resulted in commission of offences under Section 7 of E.C. Act and Sec. 3, 6 and 7 of Gas Supply Act, 2000 ?
4. What order?

13. The court's findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1-3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.
In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined the witnesses, which are as follows i.

CW1 Sri Subramani,
the informant cum the then PSI of Sanjay Nagara PS examined as PW1 deposed that on 19-10-2021,
at 9:30 am on the receipt of credible information, that the domestic gas cylinder was in illegal possession and refilled into other gas cylinders at the house bearing No.348, 3rd Main Road,
Basaveshwara Layout, Nagashettihalli and hence he along with pancha witnesses, staff raided the said house and found that the accused was refilling the gas and hence the accused was taken into custody and conducted spot cum seizure mahazar as per Ex.P1 from 10:20 am to 11:30 am.

In furtherance, rubber pipe, valve, refilling machine, 3 domestic cylinders of an Indian company, one domestic cylinder of a Bharat company, two cylinders weighing 5 kg, three cylinders weighing 3 kg,
two cylinders weighing 2 kg, weighing machine were seized and produced before CW9 and Ex.P2 report was given.
The seized properties were handed over to the Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department by obtaining the permission from the court.

He identified his signature as per Ex.P1(a) and 2(a).
ii.

CW3 Sri Khaja Husain, pancha witness examined as PW2 identified his signature on Ex.P1 mahazar and deposed that he affixed the said signature at the request of Sanjay Nagara police Station, he does not know the contents of the same, no seizure mahazar was conducted in his presence.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined this witness by treating him as hostile witness but no favorable answers has been elicited from him to support Ex.P1.

His denial of statement given before police is marked as Ex.P3.
iii.

CW6 Sri S.Nagaraj, Food Inspector examined as PW3 deposed that, on 20-10-2021, he received request from Sanjaynagar Police Station in Crime No. 240/2021 to examine and submit the report on the seized cylinders, accordingly, he examined and submitted report as per Ex.P4 by stating that Subramani M Psi vs Rafeeq Ali on 29 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120386314/

In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined these witnesses by treating them as hostile witnesses but no favorable answer have been elicited from them to support the prosecution case.

vi.

On 25-11-2021, the items seized in this case were given to the Food Department.
On 26-11-2021, the report was received as per Ex.P9 and 10, after investigation he filed charge sheet against the accused.

Further, he identified his signature as per Ex.P2(b), 7(a), 8(a), 9(a) and 10(a).
15.

A question arises whether the PW1, Police Sub-Inspector has a power to enter the house No.348,
3rd Main Road, Basaveshwara Layout, within the limits of Sanjay Nagara Police Station.

In this reference, it is relevant to mention Section 13 of the Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Supply and Distribution), 2000 which reads as under 13. Power of entry , search and seizure: (1) Any Officer of the Central or the State Government not below the rank of Inspector duly authorized by a general or a special order, by the Central Government or the State Government , as the case may be or any officer of a Government Oil Company not below the rank of Sales Officer ,
authorized by the Central Government , may , with a view to securing due compliance of this order or any other order made thereunder;
(a) Stop and search any vessel or vehicle used or capable of being used for the transport or storage of any petroleum product,
(b) enter and search any place,
(c) seize stocks of liquefied petroleum gas along with container and /or equipments , such as cylinders, gas cylinder valves, pressure regulators and seals in respect of which he has reason to believe that a contravention of this Order has been , or is being, or is about to be made.
(2) The sales officer of a Government Oil Company shall be authorised to secure compliance of this order by the distributors appointed under the public distribution system and or by the consumer Subramani M Psi vs Rafeeq Ali on 29 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120386314/
5 registered by them.
Thus, it nowhere prescribes that a Sub- Inspector of the Police can take action.

sentences.text: No doubt, the aforesaid Clause provides that in addition to the specified officers, the persons authorized by the Central or State Government may take action under the Order.
However, nothing has been placed on record to support the prosecution case that the Sub- Inspector of Police was authorized to take action under the aforesaid Order.
It is a settled law that where a power is given to do a certain thing in a certain way, the thing must be done in that way or not at all.
Other methods are necessarily forbidden and the said principle is appreciated in the case of DHARANI SUGARS AND CHEMICALS LTD. VS. UNION OF INDIA AND ORS. REPORTED IN (2019) 5 SCC 480.

PW1 has not taken any photographs or video graphed about the seizure procedure as per Ex.P1.
17.
The signature of the accused was not obtained on the seizure mahazar as per Ex.P1 to corroborate that it ws seized from his possession of the accused.
18. PW7/IO has not investigated about the source of cylinders used for refilling of gas.

19. Apart from which, Mahazar witnesses namely Khaja Husain/PW2 who is signatory to the Ex.P1 (spot cum seizure mahazar) did not support the prosecution case as he deposed that he signed at the police station.
20. The alleged eye witnesses namely PW5 and PW6 did not support the prosecution case by witnessing the incident that the accused was refilling the cylinders.
21. PW7 did not secure any document to show that the alleged spot i.e., house No.348, 3rd Main Road, Basaveshwara Layout, Bangalore belongs to accused.

22. It ought to be seen that at the time of seizure, the signature of seizure witnesses were not from local inhabitants as the spot was surrounded with the East by residential house, West by 3 rd Main Road, North by house No. 349 and south by House No. 347 however the CW2
namely

sentences.text: Whenever any place liable to search of inspection under this Chapter is closed, any person residing in, or being in charge of, such place, shall, on demand of the officer or other person executing the warrant, and on production of the warrant, allow him free ingress thereto, and afford all reasonable facilities for a search therein.

2. If ingress into such place cannot be so obtained, the officer or other person executing the warrant may proceed in the manner provided by Sub-Section (2) of section 47.
3. Where any person in or about such place is reasonably suspected of concealing about his person any article for which search should be made, such person may be searched and if such person is a woman, the search shall be made by another woman with strict regard to decency.
4. Before making a search under this Chapter, the officer or other person about to make it shall call upon two or more independent and respectable inhabitants of the locality in which the place to be searched is situate or of any other locality if no such inhabitant of the said locality is available or is willing to be a witness to the search, to attend and witness the search and may issue an order in writing to them or any of them so to do.

5. The search shall be made in their presence, and a list of all things seized in the course of such search and of the places in which they are respectively found shall be prepared by such officer or other person and signed by such witnesses; but no person witnessing a search under this section shall be required to attend the Court as a witness of the search unless specially summoned by it.
6.

The occupant of the place searched, or some person in his behalf, shall, in every instance, be permitted to attend during the search, and a copy of the list prepared under this section, signed by the said witnesses, shall be delivered to such occupant or person.
7. When any person is searched under Sub-Section (3), a list of all things taken possession of shall be prepared, and a copy thereof shall be delivered to such person.

8. Any person who, without reasonable cause, refuses or neglects to attend and witness a search under this section, when called upon to do so by an order in writing delivered or tendered to him, shall be deemed to have committed an offence under section 187 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
However the PW1/IO did not make any attempt to call the local inhabitants for the search and for drawing seizure mahazar for the alleged refilling of gas in the crime No. 240/2021.

It has been held in the case of Pradeep Narayana Vs State of Maharastra reported in AIR 1995 Supreme Court 1930 wherein it was held that failure of police to join witness from locality during search creates doubt Subramani M Psi vs Rafeeq Ali on 29 August, 2025

Thus, as discussed above by taking into account factual deficiencies in the case made out by the prosecution, the accused is entitled for benefit of doubt by an order of acquittal thereby the point No.1 to 3 is answered in negative.
24. Point No.4:-

For the foregoing discussion and the findings to the above point No.1 to 3, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Section 285, 420 of IPC and Sec.7 of E.C. Act and Sec.3, 6 and 7 of Gas Supply order,
2000.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.

(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
